chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: Scores from Town Hall and the energy of repeating them
summary: Anger drove the Vanguard music; reusing old scores costs as much energy as writing new ones.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That's right. Well, some of the energy from that undoubtedly came from anger, rage, if you want to put it that way, from all that Town Hall business.
Yeah. Yeah, because I was pooped, I after passed out at the Town Hall thing. But had held me up, it Buddy had to hold was total fatigue. But I wrote the music for that band.
What happened to the music you wrote for that Town Hall concert? Have you used it in some other context?
Yeah, I have most of the scores. But I haven't (inaudible) gone yet, going back to it again.
I mean, do you think that that music -- are you interested in giving that music another chance?
It's hard to repeat myself. Because it takes the same amount of energy (inaudible) to go through it, to go through the scores, see what's wrong, as you would have to do to --
